1.visual: A sound wave visualization made of five vertical bars of varying heights arranged symmetrically — tall bars in the center tapering down toward the outer edges — resembling an audio waveform or equalizer display.
1.usage: Audio playback interfaces to indicate a track is playing, voice message indicators in chat apps, podcast or audio player controls, audio level visualization toggles.

2.visual: A camera icon with a rounded rectangular body, a circular lens in the center, and a small raised bump on the top left representing the shutter or viewfinder. The outline style is clean with no fill.
2.usage: Photo capture buttons in camera apps, profile picture upload prompts, adding photos to a post or form, switching to camera mode in a media picker.

3.visual: A camera icon identical in shape to a standard camera (rounded body, circular lens, top bump) but with a diagonal strikethrough line crossing from the lower-left to the upper-right, indicating the camera is disabled or unavailable.
3.usage: Camera permission denied states, disabling camera in video call settings, indicating no camera detected, muting video input in a conference call.

4.visual: A rounded rectangle resembling a screen or card, containing two short horizontal lines (like text) stacked inside it — representing a caption or subtitle overlay on a display.
4.usage: Toggling subtitles or closed captions in a video player, enabling transcripts for accessibility, indicating caption settings in media playback controls, video content accessibility options.

5.visual: A film strip icon: a rounded square with two columns of small square perforations along the left and right edges, and two horizontal dividing lines inside creating three sections, representing a strip of movie film.
5.usage: Video library or media gallery navigation, adding video content, video file type indicators, accessing video editing features in a content creation tool.

6.visual: Three vertical rectangles side by side — a narrower one on the left, a taller one in the center, and a narrower one on the right — suggesting a carousel or slideshow view with a focused center slide.
6.usage: Switching to carousel or slideshow display mode, image gallery view toggles, story or card browsing interfaces, pagination controls for media content.

7.visual: A photo or image placeholder icon: a rounded square outline containing a small circle in the upper left (representing a sun or subject) and a triangular mountain silhouette in the lower right, the classic symbol for a photograph.
7.usage: Image upload placeholders, photo field indicators in forms, empty state for an image slot, thumbnail previews in media managers.

8.visual: The same photo/image icon — rounded square with a small circle and mountain silhouette — but with a diagonal strikethrough line drawn across it, indicating no image or image unavailable.
8.usage: Broken image fallback states, indicating a missing or failed-to-load photo, disabling image display in content settings, no-image-found error indicators.

9.visual: A photo icon — rounded square with a small circle and mountain silhouette — with a plus sign (+) overlaid in the upper right corner, indicating the action of adding a new image.
9.usage: Adding a photo to a post, gallery, or profile, uploading a new image in a media library, attaching an image to a message or form field, creating a new photo entry.

10.visual: Two overlapping image/photo icons — the classic rounded square with circle and mountain silhouette — stacked with one slightly offset behind the other, suggesting a collection or multiple images.
10.usage: Photo album or gallery indicators, multiple image selection in a media picker, representing an image collection or stack, batch photo operations.

11.visual: A microphone icon with a rounded rectangular capsule body at the top and a curved stand/base below it, representing the classic condenser or studio microphone shape in outline style.
11.usage: Voice recording controls, speech-to-text input activation, unmuting a microphone in a call interface, podcast or audio recording tools.

12.visual: The same microphone icon — capsule body with curved stand — but with a diagonal strikethrough line crossing over it, indicating the microphone is muted or disabled.
12.usage: Mute microphone button in video or audio calls, indicating microphone is off or permission denied, muted state in a voice chat interface, disabling voice input.

13.visual: A musical note icon showing two eighth notes joined by a horizontal beam at the top, each with a filled oval note head and a vertical stem, the standard music symbol.
13.usage: Music playback controls or players, indicating audio or music content in a list, toggling background music in an app, linking to a music library or playlist.

14.visual: A podcast or radio broadcast icon: a person silhouette at the bottom center with two sets of concentric curved arcs radiating outward above them on both sides, representing signal transmission or broadcasting.
14.usage: Podcast app navigation or episode listings, live radio or streaming broadcast indicators, subscribing to a podcast feed, broadcasting or going live in a creator tool.

15.visual: A video camera icon with a rounded rectangular body on the left and a triangular arrow or lens element pointing inward on the right side, representing a camcorder in outline style.
15.usage: Starting a video call or recording, switching to video mode, indicating video content in a feed, video chat or conferencing controls.

16.visual: The same video camera icon — rectangular body with the triangular right-side element — but with a diagonal strikethrough line crossing over it, indicating video is disabled or camera is turned off.
16.usage: Turning off video in a conference call, video camera muted or unavailable state, disabling video capture, indicating no video permission granted.
